newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga says not threatened by power deal.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga says not threatened by power deal.

text.p: Malaysia's state power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd did not feel threatened by the break in its monopoly on power distribution with the award of a contract to a private firm this week, a local newspaper reported on Wednesday.

In an interview with Business Times, Tenaga executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali dismissed a suggestion that the deal signals a change in the direction of the electricity industry or a change in government policy.

"The decision was made in late 1995 or early 1996...this was just a follow through. The licence award is not anything new. Since I took over (in September 1996), I have not been made aware of any change in government policy that would have any negative effect on the outlook for Tenaga," he said.
"On the contrary, all policy announcements made since September have been positive to Tenaga," Tajuddin added.
The government on Monday issued a licence to a consortium led by Manfield Development Sdn Bhd to generate and distribute power to a high-technology industrial park in northern Kedah state.

Tajuddin said this will not be the first electricity project to be handled by a private company. Others include the award of the power transmission contract to EPE Distribution Sdn Bhd, a unit of EPE Power Corp Bhd for the light rail transit system, he said.

Tajuddin said there will be two or three more developments in the near future that might be construed as negative to Tenaga. "But these are old stories and have been discounted for as far as Tenaga's outlook is concerned,' he said.
Worries that Tenaga could lose its distribution monopoly pushed the stock down 50 cents to close at 12.40 ringgit on Tuesday.
